items.title: Danny Barker Interview (Louis Armstrong memorial broadcast), 1971-07-09
items.q: A marvelous wife, Lucille, whom he met at the Cotton Club.

ctx.x: I see trees of green, red and blue and stew. I see them bloom, from me and you. And I think to myself, what a wonderful world. What a wonderful world. I see skies of blue and clouds of white. The bright, blessed day. The bright, blessed day. The dark, sacred night. And I think to myself, what a wonderful world. What a wonderful world. The colors of the rainbow. So pretty in the sky. Are also on the faces of people going by. I see friends shaking in. Saying, how do you do? They're really saying, I love you. I hear…

Now, Louis Armstrong's wonderful world is just a little of Louis' Fred Robbins. I'm so glad I went to see Louis Armstrong on Sunday, his birthday, 71st, at his home in Corona. I never would have forgiven myself if I hadn't. I was on the way back from the beach and we called, of course, in advance to find out if he was okay. And his wonderful wife, Lucille, said, sure, drop in. I'd been at his home several times before on his birthday. But this was the most important. He looked fine. His face was fuller. He was…
